analysis:
Reviewed the supplied head text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1217-2025) against the canonical threat model. The file is documentation only, and the changed range in file_changes is head 3541-3575. That range falls outside both supplied units, so the new 'Cluster service listeners follow the cable and the pairing' section is not visible here. Its patch excerpt is truncated at the end, so I cannot verify the change itself or any code behind it.

The supplied text describes existing behavior: GLM5 vision and tool parsing, startup calibration, prefix-cache and SSD stage ordering, deadlines and MTP. It makes no new security claims that weaken T-041, T-008, T-010 or T-053. For example, the ChunkBatcher paragraph (lines 1547-1559) states that SendHandle and ChunkSender persist across reconnects and that there is no request-to-session identity enforcement. This is documented candidly and is not a regression introduced here.

The new cluster-listener text is a pairing-keyed listener that refuses handshakes from a later pairing. It touches a cluster and distributed pairing surface that the threat model does not cover with any trust boundary. That is a possible threat-model gap for a later pass, since the visible text does not show the code. I cannot confirm an actual regression. The next pass should examine ClusterService.listenerChange and ensureResponder in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Distributed/Onboarding/ClusterService.swift. It should check that a listener restart cannot be used to downgrade pairing, and that the listener does not bind a broader address than the cable's.
